intro: New Zealand has two main islands with mountains, volcanoes, glaciers, fjords and beaches.

chapters.title: North and South
text: The North Island has volcanoes like Ruapehu and geothermal areas around Rotorua. The South Island has the Southern Alps, with Aoraki/Mount Cook at 3,724 m, and fjords like Milford Sound.
New Zealand sits on the boundary of two tectonic plates, so earthquakes are common; Christchurch was badly damaged in 2011.

chapters.title: Unique wildlife
text: Before humans arrived there were no land mammals except bats. Birds like the kiwi, kākāpō and takahē evolved there, many flightless.

keyTerms.meaning: A deep sea inlet carved by glaciers.
